page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-32 is a compute-optimized server instance featuring 32 vCPUs and 64 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-per-core ratio. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled and dedicated CPU allocation. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance in specific computational tasks. The instance achieves top-tier performance in Geekbench text processing and small-model LLM text generation. Strong performance is also observed in single-threaded gzip compression, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench image processing. Standard CPU and memory operations, such as Passmark CPU and Redis SET operations, fall within the average range.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is designed for compute-bound workloads where memory density is not the primary constraint. This resource allocation provides qualitative cost efficiency for CPU-intensive tasks by avoiding the overhead of unutilized memory. The presence of advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, makes it suitable for CPU-based machine learning inference, text processing, web serving, and data decompression tasks.
